title: Aider
summary: A terminal-based AI pair-programming tool whose Git workflow and model-provider costs need separate review.

facts.label: Workflow
facts.value: AI pair programming in a terminal, working with a local code repository.

facts.label: Git workflow
facts.value: Creates commits for edits; the docs say it first commits pre-existing dirty changes and skips Git hooks by default unless configured otherwise.

facts.label: Model providers
facts.value: Connects to multiple cloud providers and can use local models; provider and model capability vary.

facts.label: Local model inference
facts.value: Local models are supported through compatible model providers; validate capability and hardware independently.

facts.label: Privacy / data handling
facts.value: Aider's analytics documentation says it asks a random subset of users to opt in when neither analytics switch is supplied; collection begins only after agreement. It lists selected LLMs and token counts, edit formats, feature/command use and errors linked to a random UUID4, and says these analytics exclude code, prompts/chat messages, API keys and personal information. Users can disable a session with --no-analytics or permanently with --analytics-disable. This describes Aider's product analytics only; review the selected model provider's data terms separately.

facts.label: Code / data portability
facts.value: Git-managed repository changes can be inspected and reverted with Git.

facts.label: Repository license
facts.value: The public Aider repository identifies an Apache-2.0 license; model and provider terms are separate.

prices.name: Model/provider usage
prices.billing: Provider charges depend on the selected model and usage; confirm the current provider route.

sections.heading: Make the Git behavior part of the trial
paragraphs: Use a disposable branch with a failing test and a narrowly scoped task. The docs say Aider commits pre-existing dirty changes before editing and skips Git hooks by default unless configured otherwise. Inspect commit behavior, enable the required hook verification and rehearse undo before using an established repository.

sections.heading: Budget the model separately
paragraphs: Choose a provider and model before estimating cost. Record the provider's billing unit and the usage produced by your task; local model support does not establish adequate quality or zero operating cost.

pros.text: Each edited file is committed with a descriptive message, making changes reviewable and reversible through Git.
The documentation covers multiple hosted model providers and local models through Ollama or OpenAI-compatible APIs.

cons.text: Aider commits pre-existing dirty files before editing and skips Git pre-commit hooks by default unless configured otherwise.
Model capability varies; Aider warns that less capable models may fail to return edits it can apply.

faqs.question: Can Aider use a local model?
faqs.answer: Yes. The docs describe using local models through Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible local API; confirm the model's editing capability in your own trial.

faqs.question: What should I check before the first edit?
faqs.answer: Review the dirty-file commit and hook defaults, then trial on a disposable branch so the Git effects are visible.

verdict: Evaluate Aider when a terminal and Git-centered pair-programming loop fits your repository work. Verify model quality, provider spend and commit behavior in a bounded trial.
bestFor: Developers comfortable reviewing terminal output and Git changes
notFor: Teams expecting a single fixed product price or unreviewed autonomous changes
migration: Preserve repository instructions and provider configuration separately. Trial on a branch, keep credentials in the approved secret store and verify the resulting diff before merging.
gaps: Confirm current provider billing and whether any separate hosted or commercial offering applies to the intended use.
Confirm the installed Aider version and analytics consent/configuration; no local settings were inspected.
Review privacy, retention, training and jurisdiction terms for the selected model provider; Aider's analytics policy does not determine provider handling.
Confirm Git hook behavior and protect pre-existing dirty changes before a trial.
Do not treat repository license as a license for model weights or provider services.
